flags.detail: The overall synthesis rests on placing SSB ingredients (order parameter, potential, vacua) that exist on a Q(sqrt5) 'face' and object-specificity (class group) that exists on a Q(sqrt-3) 'face' into a single narrative via B261's claim that 'one AJ operator carries both ends' -- explicitly flagged by the arc itself as 'an analogy and not a result... needs its own gate before it carries anything', so the synthesis's physical interpretation (that this is one coherent SSB mechanism) is presently a structural coincidence across two number fields rather than a demonstrated single mechanism.

The representation-content menus at each cascade step (which irreps the 27/16/10+5bar decompose into under each candidate subgroup) are entered as hardcoded data matching standard GUT branching tables, not computed from an explicit embedding/root-system construction within this script -- a type-match against textbook group theory rather than an independent derivation.

The core claim is a dimension/structure match (so(8)+u(1)^2+3x16, dim 78) between the repo's build and a classical named object (M(O,C)); FINDINGS.md itself records that a secondary source's competing claim ('tri(C)=so(3)') was caught purely by dimension arithmetic (28+3+48 != 78), which is exactly the kind of type-coincidence reasoning this seat is asked to flag as a license to ask, not evidence -- though in this case the repo's own check correctly used it to REJECT a wrong identification rather than accept one, which is the right use.

the original claim ('takes E6 to the Standard Model algebra') is off by construction: the computed object is 14-dimensional with THREE abelian factors, while the real Standard Model gauge algebra su(3)+su(2)+u(1) is 12-dimensional with ONE abelian factor -- a category error between 'a Levi subalgebra containing the SM factors' and 'the SM algebra itself', caught two corrections later (B950, B951) but never repaired in this arc's own verdict file

test_w4_theorem_recheck_from_the_tower_pickle's own comment admits the pickle isn't available in this environment and the 'recheck' is just re-reading the same results.json field ('identically zero' string), not an independent recomputation from the pickle as the name implies.

The arc's own law-status classification (creates_law: false) was performed by a later arc (B1214) that explicitly did NOT read this arc in full before flipping its classification, per its own stated basis field -- a downgrade made on a headline read, not a full audit.
